anf_compare.notes: No ANF or other public-domain English of this homily; translated from the Greek.

bible_refs.note: Ἀπέδρα … ὀδύνη καὶ λύπη καὶ στεναγμός matches LXX Isaiah 35:10 (ἀπέδρα ὀδύνη καὶ λύπη καὶ στεναγμός); the same line recurs at Isaiah 51:11. The first occurrence is cited. Verse numbering is the same in LXX and Hebrew.

Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν θεοῦ, ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο follows Romans 11:34 (Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν κυρίου; ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο;) with γάρ and ἤ; Paul quotes LXX Isaiah 40:13 (τίς ἔγνω νοῦν κυρίου, καὶ τίς αὐτοῦ σύμβουλος ἐγένετο). Hesychius has θεοῦ for κυρίου; the English follows him ('the mind of God').

Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ καὶ τὰ παιδία ἅ μοι δέδωκας, ὦ θεός adapts Hebrews 2:13 / LXX Isaiah 8:18 (Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ καὶ τὰ παιδία ἅ μοι ἔδωκεν ὁ θεός), turned into address to the Father ('you have given me, O God'). Hebrews puts the words in Christ's mouth, which is how Hesychius uses them, so Hebrews is cited first.
Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου matches LXX Psalm 109:1 exactly, Hebrew/English Psalm 110:1; LXX numbering converted.

choices.english: through his being carried in the womb
choices.why: κύησις is pregnancy; 'his' makes plain it is Christ's own gestation, as the parallel διὰ τῆς ἀναστάσεως (his resurrection) requires.
ἄλειπτος ('unanointed') does not fit; read as the itacistic spelling of ἄληπτος. The copy-text is not emended.
Here the proclamation of joy on Easter day; 'Annunciation' would point to the feast of 25 March.

choices.english: he was born for the sake of man
choices.why: διά with the accusative gives the reason, not the means.

lemmas.gloss: the dead, those put to death

pass_a_gloss: [continuing from u01-rem-mid: 'For this one was hidden first'] on the one hand in womb of flesh, then in womb of the earth, where on the one hand sanctifying those being born through the conception / gestation, where on the other making alive those put to death through the resurrection. 'For fled away pain and grief and groaning.' 'For who knew mind of God, or who became his counsellor', except the Word, the one made flesh and nailed to wood and risen from the dead and exalted into heavens? This the day of joy good-news announcement; for in this day rose the Lord, having raised together the flock of Adam; for he was born because of the human and rose in the human. Today through the one who rose paradise has been opened and Adam is made alive and Eve is consoled and calling is multiplied and kingdom is prepared and human is saved and Christ is worshipped; for having trampled down death and having taken captive the tyrant and having despoiled Hades, he went up into heavens, as king having conquered, as leader / commander glorious, as charioteer unovertaken, saying to the Father: 'Behold I and the children whom to me you have given, O God,' and the following. And he heard from the Father: 'Sit at right of me until I place your enemies footstool of your feet.' To him the glory, now and into the ages of the ages. Amen. [Page marker '2' omitted.]
pass_b_english: …in a womb of flesh, and then in the womb of the earth: in the one, sanctifying those who are born, through his being carried in the womb; in the other, giving life to the dead, through his resurrection. 'For pain and sorrow and sighing have fled away' (Isaiah 35:10). 'For who has known the mind of God, or who has been his counselor?' (Romans 11:34; Isaiah 40:13) Who, except the Word, who became flesh, was nailed to the wood, rose from the dead, and was lifted up into the heavens?
This day is the good news of joy. For on this day the Lord rose, and raised with him the flock of Adam. For he was born for the sake of man, and he rose in man.

Today, through the one who rose, paradise has been opened, Adam is given life, Eve is comforted, the calling is multiplied, the kingdom is made ready, man is saved, and Christ is worshipped. For he trampled down death, took the tyrant captive, and plundered Hades, and then he went up into the heavens as a victorious king, as a glorious commander, as a charioteer never overtaken, saying to the Father, 'Here am I, and the children whom you have given me, O God' (Hebrews 2:13; Isaiah 8:18), and the rest. And he heard from the Father, 'Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet' (Psalm 110:1).
To him be the glory, now and to the ages of ages. Amen.
source_text:
μὲν ἐν κοιλίᾳ σαρκός, ἔπειτα δὲ ἐν κοιλίᾳ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου μὲν ἁγιάζων τοὺς
γεννωμένους διὰ τῆς κυήσεως, ὅπου δὲ ζωογονῶν τοὺς τεθανατωμένους διὰ τῆς
ἀναστάσεως· «Ἀπέδρα γὰρ ὀδύνη καὶ λύπη καὶ στεναγμός.» «Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν
θεοῦ, ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο», ἀλλ' ἢ ὁ Λόγος ὁ σαρκωθεὶς καὶ ξύλῳ
προσηλωθεὶς καὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστὰς καὶ εἰς οὐρανοὺς ὑψωθείς;
6 Αὕτη ἡ ἡμέρα χαρᾶς εὐαγγελισμός· ἐν τῇ γὰρ ἡμέρᾳ ταύτῃ ἀνέστη ὁ κύριος
συνεγείρας τὴν τοῦ Ἀδὰμ ἀγέλην· ἐγεννήθη γὰρ διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ ἀνέστη ἐν τῷ
ἀνθρώπῳ. Σήμερον διὰ τὸν ἀναστάντα παράδεισος ἀνέῳκται καὶ Ἀδὰμ ζωογονεῖται
καὶ Εὔα παρηγορεῖται καὶ κλῆσις πληθύνεται καὶ βασιλεία ἑτοιμάζεται καὶ ἄνθρωπος
σῴζεται καὶ Χριστὸς προσκυνεῖται· καταπατήσας γὰρ τὸν θάνατον καὶ αἰχμαλωτίσας
τὸν τύραννον καὶ σκυλεύσας τὸν ᾅδην, ἀνέβη εἰς οὐρανούς, ὡς βα σιλεὺς
νενικηκώς, ὡς ἡγεμὼν ἔνδοξος, ὡς ἡνίοχος ἄλειπτος, λέ-γων τῷ Πατρί· «Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ
καὶ τὰ παιδία ἅ μοι δέδωκας, ὦ θεός», καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. Καὶ ἤκουσεν παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός·
«Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.»
Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα, νῦν καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.

2
source_normalizations: Line-break splits joined (βα σιλεὺς, λέ-γων); no letters added.
The trailing page number '2' is an editorial page marker and is not translated.
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Row opens mid-sentence ('…in a womb of flesh'), completing 'For he was hidden, first…' at the end of u01-rem-mid, and runs to the doxology and Amen.

Every clause checked against the Greek: the two hidings (womb of flesh, womb of the earth), the two quotations and Hesychius's answer, the day of good news, the seven present passives of the Easter list, the three conquests, the ascent with the three similes, the words to the Father and the Father's reply, and the doxology.

Reviewer fix applied in tr0: both halves of ὅπου μὲν … ὅπου δὲ now name Christ's own acts ('through his being carried in the womb'; 'through his resurrection'), with commas keeping the means attached to the participle.

Scripture checked: Isaiah 35:10, Romans 11:34 with Isaiah 40:13, Hebrews 2:13 with Isaiah 8:18, Psalm 110:1 (LXX Psalm 109:1, numbering converted). Matthew 12:40, John 1:14, Luke 2:10, Matthew 25:34 and LXX Psalm 67:19 are possible echoes only.
